sub: Named after “the clear evidence” (al-bayyinah) at the end of ayah 1
theme: Why a Messenger had to come: people would not leave disbelief until clear proof arrived. The true religion was always sincere worship, prayer and zakah, and people end up as the worst or the best of creation.
story: Where it was revealed is disputed: either Makkah or Madinah, and nothing in its content settles it. It follows Al-ʿAlaq, the first revelation, and Al-Qadr, the night it came, and explains why a Messenger had to come with that Book.

The People of the Book had been waiting for a promised final prophet. When he came with clear proof, they split: some believed, and many rejected him. The idol-worshippers, too, stayed in their ways until the proof reached them.
The Prophet ﷺ once told Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that Allah had commanded him to recite this surah to him. Ubayy asked, “He named me?” When told yes, he wept.

sections.title: Clear proof, the Messenger, came; they split, though told to worship sincerely
sections.meaning: The disbelievers among the People of the Book and the idol-worshippers would not let go of their error until clear proof came: a Messenger reciting purified pages of upright rulings. The People of the Book split only after it came, though they were only ever commanded to worship Allah sincerely, pray and give zakah.
points: They would not leave disbelief until the clear proof came
The proof: a Messenger reciting purified pages of upright writings
The People of the Book split only after the proof came
The command was always sincere worship, prayer and zakah
sections.matters: It explains why a Messenger was needed, and it sums up the religion in one ayah: worship Allah alone and sincerely, pray, and give zakah. People did not split for lack of guidance; they split after it came.
sections.story: No specific incident. The People of the Book had agreed a final prophet was coming. When he arrived, they divided over him: some believed, and others rejected him, some out of envy.
explained: Munfakkīn: they would not let go. People of the Book and idol-worshippers alike stayed in their error, the years only adding to it, until al-bayyinah came. That clear proof is the Messenger ﷺ, reciting ṣuḥuf muṭahharah, pages kept pure from falsehood, holding kutub qayyimah: upright rulings and true reports.

The People of the Book did not split for lack of guidance. They split after the proof came. Yet every scripture carried the same command: worship Allah with ikhlāṣ, as ḥunafāʾ turning from every false way, pray and give zakah. That is dīn al-qayyimah, the straight religion.
teaches: Guidance came clearly; whoever splits from it after that is responsible.
Ikhlāṣ, sincerity to Allah, is the core of all worship.
Prayer and zakah stand at the centre of the religion.
The Quran is pure, and its rulings are straight and just.
sections.hook: Al-bayyinah ends ayah 1 and ayah 4; qayyimah ends ayah 3 and ayah 5. Ayah 1 names two groups, ayah 4 only one. The section fills the rest of page 598.

sections.title: Disbelievers are worst of creation in Hell; believers are best, in Gardens
sections.meaning: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the idol-worshippers will be in Hell forever: the worst of creation. Those who believe and do good are the best of creation. Their reward is gardens forever, with Allah pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.
points: Disbelievers of both groups: Hell forever, worst of creation
Believers who do good: best of creation
Gardens forever; Allah pleased with them, they pleased with Him
All this is for whoever stands in awe of his Lord
sections.matters: After the proof comes the outcome. The same two groups from ayah 1 return, now judged by how they answered it. The highest reward named is not the gardens but Allah’s pleasure, and it is tied to awe of Him.
sections.story: No specific incident. It completes the surah: once the clear proof has come, people are sorted by how they responded to it.
explained: Those who rejected the proof, from the People of the Book and the idol-worshippers, are in Hell forever, with no way out. They are sharr al-bariyyah, the worst of creation, because they knew the truth and left it. Those who believed in their hearts and acted with their bodies are khayr al-bariyyah, the best of creation.

Their reward is jannāt ʿadn, gardens of permanent stay with rivers flowing beneath, without end. Greater than all of it: Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him for all He gave. This is for whoever has khashyah, an awe of his Lord that keeps him obeying and away from sin.
teaches: Knowing the truth and turning away from it is what makes the worst of creation.
Faith in the heart must show in deeds.
Allah’s pleasure is greater than every delight of Paradise.
Khashyah, awe of Allah, leads to obedience, not just fear.
sections.hook: Ayah 6 repeats the words of ayah 1: alladhīna kafarū min ahl al-kitāb wal-mushrikīn. Ayat 6 and 7 mirror each other: sharr al-bariyyah, then khayr al-bariyyah. Page 599 starts at ayah 6.

groups.text: People would not leave their error until clear proof came: a Messenger reciting purified pages of upright rulings.
The People of the Book split only after the proof came, though they were commanded only to worship Allah sincerely, pray and give zakah.
The disbelievers of both groups are the worst of creation, in Hell forever; believers who do good are the best of creation.
Gardens forever, Allah pleased with them and they with Him: this is for whoever fears his Lord.

1.explain: Munfakkīn: they would not let go of their error. The People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the idol-worshippers stayed as they were until al-bayyinah, the clear proof, came.

2.explain: The clear proof is the Messenger ﷺ, reciting ṣuḥuf muṭahharah: pages kept pure from falsehood. He recited from memory what was preserved in written pages.

3.explain: Inside those pages are kutub qayyimah: upright rulings and true reports with nothing crooked in them, guiding to the straight path.

4.explain: The People of the Book had agreed a prophet was coming. When the proof arrived, they split over him: some believed, and others rejected him out of envy.

5.explain: Every scripture gave the same command: worship Allah with ikhlāṣ, as ḥunafāʾ turning away from shirk, pray and give zakah. These two are named for their high rank. That is the straight religion.

6.explain: Those who rejected the proof are in Hell forever, with no way out. They are sharr al-bariyyah, the worst of creation, because they knew the truth and left it.

7.explain: Those who believe with their hearts and do good with their bodies are khayr al-bariyyah, the best of all creation.

8.explain: Jannāt ʿadn: gardens of permanent stay. Allah being pleased with them outweighs every other delight, and they are pleased with Him. It is for those with khashyah, awe that keeps them obeying.
